witness.why: 4 != 1 mod 13, and n = 14 lies in the claim's stated domain [0, 40].
witness.root_cause: The multiplicative order of 2 modulo 13 is 12, not 14 (2^12 = 4096 = 315*13+1). Step s2 asserts order 14 and is false; 2^14 = 4 mod 13, so reduction of the exponent mod 14 is not exponent-reduction for this modulus. The correct reduction is n mod 12.
witness.all_counterexamples_in_domain: every n with 14 <= n <= 40 (27 of the 41 cases); the claim holds only on 0 <= n <= 13, where n mod 14 = n trivially

search_bound: exhaustive over the entire stated domain n in [0, 40] (41 cases); this is the full domain, not a bounded sample
notes: Steps s3, s4, s5, s7, s8, s9, s10 are true but irrelevant filler (statements about n^3 - n mod 6, an indicator-function identity, triangular-number parity, etc.) with fabricated dependency edges to the modular claim; s6 is false as stated for the same reason as s2 (14 | n does not force 2^n = 1 mod 13; n = 14 gives 4). The claim is FALSE outright, so no TRUE_BUT_INVALID_ARGUMENT disposition applies.
